core_obligations: Settle the degenerate cases and choose a nonzero element of the prime, then apply a change of coordinates making it monic in one variable so that the corresponding quotient map is finite (proof lines 28300-28325).
Apply the induction hypothesis in one fewer variable to control the contraction of the prime there, and compose the two maps to obtain the required normalization (proof lines 28325-28339).
proof_roadmap: Normalise the form of a chosen element by a change of coordinates (proof lines 28299-28325).
Induct on the number of variables and compose the maps (proof lines 28325-28340).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a prime in a polynomial ring over a field there is a finite map from another polynomial ring whose contraction of the prime is a coordinate subspace of the expected dimension (statement lines 28290-28297). The proof does not quote Noether normalization: it inducts on the number of variables, first applying a change of coordinates that makes a chosen element of the prime monic in one variable, then uses the induction hypothesis in one fewer variable and composes (proof lines 28299-28340). The coordinate change that produces finiteness is the step that carries the induction. H2.
